items.title: Locality of cohomology: a cohomology class on a site dies on a covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter etale-cohomology.tex, section on locality of cohomology
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any site C, abelian sheaf F, object U, degree p > 0 and class xi in H^p(U, F) there is a covering of U over which xi restricts to zero (statement lines 2256-2260). The proof has to move once from the class to a representative and once from the representative to local primitives, and the second move is available precisely because p > 0 makes the resolution exact at I^p, so a section of the kernel sheaf becomes a coboundary after restriction to a covering (proof lines 2264-2271). The statement is then immediate from the fact that the restriction of a class is computed from the restriction of its representative. The claim is H2: the same two-step use of an injective resolution as in the ringed-site version, with its own self-contained proof in this chapter.
